t: Rajesh sold his insured house to Kumar on 1 March. On 15 March a fire damaged the house while Rajesh's fire policy was still in force. Rajesh's claim is:
o: Payable, since the policy was in force
Not payable, since Rajesh had no insurable interest at the time of loss
Payable in part to Rajesh and in part to Kumar
e: In property insurance, insurable interest must exist at the time of loss; having sold the house, Rajesh suffers no financial loss.

t: Under IRDAI regulations, a licensed surveyor should ordinarily submit the survey report to the insurer within how many days of appointment?
e: The IRDAI (Insurance Surveyors and Loss Assessors) Regulations require the report within 30 days, extendable in special cases.

t: Under a 'family floater' health policy:
o: Each member has a separate sum insured
Only the eldest member is covered
One sum insured is shared by all the insured family members
Premium is paid by the Government
e: In a floater, the single sum insured floats over all members and can be used by any one or more of them during the year.

t: Premium rates for most classes of general insurance in India were freed from tariff control (detariffing) with effect from:
e: The Tariff Advisory Committee's tariffs for fire, engineering, motor own-damage and other classes were withdrawn from 1 January 2007, allowing insurers to set their own rates.

t: Six months into an annual fire policy, the insured increases the sum insured by Rs 10 lakh by endorsement. The additional premium is normally charged:
o: Pro rata for the unexpired six months
Not at all, as the policy is already in force
e: Additional premium for a mid-term increase is charged on a pro rata basis for the remaining period of the policy.

t: In marine insurance, the requirement that the vessel be seaworthy at the commencement of the voyage is an example of:
e: Implied warranties (seaworthiness, legality of voyage) are not written in the policy but are implied by law.

t: Since the Insurance Laws (Amendment) Act, 2015, individual insurance agents are:
o: Appointed by insurers, which maintain their records, instead of being licensed by IRDAI
Licensed directly by IRDAI as before
Appointed by the Life Insurance Council
Required to be registered with SEBI
e: The 2015 amendment substituted Section 42, shifting agent appointment to insurers under IRDAI regulations.

t: Before the Insurance Act, 1938, which legislation specifically regulated life insurance business in India?
e: The 1912 Act was the first statute to regulate life insurance; general insurance was first brought under statistical control by the Indian Insurance Companies Act, 1928.

t: Following the opening up of the insurance sector, the General Insurance Corporation of India was re-designated in the year 2000 as the:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). In November 2000 GIC was notified as the Indian reinsurer and ceased direct underwriting; its four subsidiaries were later delinked in 2002.

t: A shopkeeper deliberately sets fire to unsold stock in order to collect the insurance money. This illustrates:
e: Moral hazard arises from dishonesty or bad character of the insured, such as deliberately causing a loss or inflating a claim.

t: Ram's stock is insured with X and Y for equal sums insured. Unaware of the other policy, X pays Ram's full loss of Rs 50,000. X can recover from Y:
e: Under contribution, an insurer that has paid more than its rateable share can recover the excess from the co-insurer; here Y's share is half.

t: A personal accident policy pays a weekly benefit to an insured who, after an accident, is unable to attend to his occupation for 10 weeks and then fully recovers. This benefit is for:
e: PA policies pay a weekly sum for temporary total disablement and lump sums for death and permanent disablement.

t: When life insurance was nationalised in 1956, about how many Indian and foreign insurers and provident societies were merged to form LIC?
e: LIC was formed by amalgamating 245 Indian and foreign insurers and provident societies; 107 general insurers were later merged into four companies in 1972-73.

t: Risks arising from changes in the economy, technology or consumer tastes are known as:
e: Dynamic risks result from changes in the economy and society, whereas static risks such as fire or theft occur even in an unchanging economy.

t: Under the standard fire policy in India, after giving immediate notice of loss, the insured must deliver a written claim with full particulars within:
e: The claims condition requires a detailed written claim within 15 days of the loss, unless the insurer extends the time.

t: Which section of the Insurance Act, 1938 requires that premium be received in advance before an insurer assumes any risk?
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Section 64VB lays down the 'no risk without premium' rule, so cover commences only after the premium is received by the insurer.

t: A bank insists that a house financed by it be insured against fire. The main reason is that insurance:
o: Prevents the house from catching fire
Increases the market value of the house
Is compulsory under the Insurance Act for all houses
Protects the security against which the loan is given
e: Insurance enhances credit by protecting the lender's security, enabling businesses and individuals to obtain finance.

t: Mohan and Sohan are partners in a business. Mohan proposes a life policy on Sohan's life. The proposal is:
o: Acceptable, as partners have insurable interest in each other's lives
Not acceptable, as only blood relatives can insure each other
Not acceptable, as only the person himself can insure his own life
Acceptable only if Sohan is Mohan's employee
e: Business partners have a financial interest in each other's continued life and hence possess insurable interest.

t: In marine cargo insurance, a certificate of insurance is normally issued:
o: Only when a claim is lodged
For each shipment declared under an open cover or open policy
e: Under an open cover the insurer issues a certificate for each declared consignment, which serves as evidence of insurance for banks and buyers.

t: General insurance contracts are described as 'personal contracts' because:
o: They cover only persons and not property
The insurer relies on the character of the insured, so the policy cannot be transferred without the insurer's consent
They are signed personally by the Chairman
They are issued only to individuals
e: Since the insurer assesses the insured's moral hazard, the contract is personal and assignment of a general insurance policy needs the insurer's consent.

t: A chemical manufacturer decides never to produce a highly explosive compound because of the danger involved. This is an example of:
e: Avoidance eliminates the exposure altogether by not undertaking the activity that creates it.

t: A cover note issued pending preparation of the policy is generally valid for a limited period not exceeding:
e: A cover note is temporary evidence of cover; it is generally valid for up to 60 days, within which the policy should be issued.

t: 'Adverse selection' (anti-selection) in insurance refers to:
o: Insurers selecting only the best risks
The tendency of persons with higher-than-average risk to seek insurance more eagerly
The choice of a wrong insurer by the customer
The selection of a wrong sum insured
e: Underwriting exists to counter adverse selection, where poor risks are more likely to buy insurance at standard rates.

t: Under Section 30 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, which type of agreement is declared void?
e: Wagering agreements are void; insurance is distinguished from a wager by the presence of insurable interest.

t: When an insurer itself cancels a general insurance policy mid-term, the premium refund is normally calculated:
o: Pro rata for the unexpired period
e: Cancellation by the insurer attracts a pro rata refund, whereas cancellation by the insured is on short period rates.

t: Stock worth Rs 15 lakh is insured against burglary at a rate of Rs 3 per mille. GST is 18%. The total amount payable by the insured is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Premium = 15,00,000 x 3/1000 = Rs 4,500; GST at 18% = Rs 810; total Rs 5,310.

t: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority was renamed 'Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India' (IRDAI) by:
e: The 2015 amendment changed the name of the regulator to IRDAI, besides raising the foreign investment cap and strengthening penalties.

t: Which of the following is an example of a pure risk?
o: Destruction of a warehouse by fire
Fall in the price of shares bought as an investment
Loss on the launch of a new product
Betting on the outcome of a cricket match
e: A pure risk offers only the possibility of loss or no loss, with no chance of gain; the other options involve a possibility of gain and are speculative.

t: In reinsurance terminology, the 'cedant' or 'ceding company' is:
o: The reinsurer that accepts the risk
The direct insurer that passes on part of its risk to a reinsurer
e: The insurer which cedes (transfers) risk is the cedant; the party accepting it is the reinsurer.

t: Estimating how often losses are likely to occur and how severe they may be is part of which step of the risk management process?
o: Selection of the risk handling technique
e: After exposures are identified, they are evaluated in terms of probable frequency and severity so that the right technique can be chosen.

t: An underwriter accepts a factory with inadequate fire-fighting arrangements but at a rate higher than the standard. This underwriting decision is:
e: Underwriters may accept at normal rates, accept with loading/excess/special conditions, postpone, or decline.

t: A policy carries a franchise of Rs 5,000. A loss of Rs 7,000 occurs. The insurer pays:
e: Under a franchise, once the loss exceeds the franchise amount the whole loss is paid; under an excess only the amount above the excess is paid.

t: A standard fire policy provides that if the insurer repudiates a claim and the insured does not commence legal proceedings within a stated period, the claim is deemed abandoned. That period is:
o: 12 months from the date of repudiation
e: The disclaimer condition requires suit or legal action within 12 calendar months of rejection, failing which the claim is treated as abandoned.

t: An Insurance Ombudsman can entertain a complaint where the value of the claim, including expenses, does not exceed:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The limit was raised to ₹50 lakh by the amended Insurance Ombudsman Rules.

t: A life insurance plan that pays a part of the sum assured at fixed intervals during the term and the balance with bonus on maturity is a:
e: Money-back (anticipated endowment) plans provide periodic survival benefits while keeping full life cover during the term.

t: Which of the following perils is NOT covered under the Standard Fire and Special Perils policy in India?
e: War risks are excluded from all property policies; lightning, STFI and RSMD are named perils of the standard fire policy.

t: Under a reinstatement value fire policy, the basis of settlement for destroyed machinery is:
o: The original purchase price paid years ago
The cost of replacing it with new machinery of the same kind, without deduction for depreciation
Book value as per the balance sheet
e: Reinstatement value policies are a modification of strict indemnity and pay 'new for old', subject to actual reinstatement.

t: The 'peace of mind' that insurance offers is valuable to the economy mainly because it:
o: Frees businessmen from worry and encourages enterprise and investment
Reduces the number of accidents in factories
Guarantees that no business will ever fail
Removes the need for banks and lenders
e: By relieving anxiety about potential losses, insurance encourages people to undertake productive ventures.

t: A marine hull policy under which the insurer and insured fix the value of the vessel at inception, and that value is paid on total loss, is a:
e: Valued policies are an exception to strict indemnity; the agreed value is paid irrespective of actual value at the time of loss.

t: Under IRDAI guidelines, an insurer must designate an officer to deal with policyholders' complaints, known as the:
e: Every insurer must have a Grievance Redressal Officer at head office and at every branch, and a board-approved grievance policy.

t: An insurer pays Rs 50,000 to its insured for damage caused by a third party and then recovers Rs 60,000 from that third party. The excess Rs 10,000:
o: Belongs to the insurer as profit
Must be paid to the Government
Is shared equally between insurer and insured
e: Subrogation entitles the insurer only to the amount it has paid; any excess recovery is held for the insured.

t: The Insurance Information Bureau of India (IIB) was set up by IRDA primarily to:
o: Collect, analyse and disseminate industry-wide insurance data
e: IIB (2009) is the data repository for the Indian insurance sector, supporting pricing, fraud detection and policy decisions.

t: The IRDAI portal through which a policyholder can escalate an unresolved grievance against an insurer is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Bima Bharosa (formerly IGMS) is the grievance portal; Bima Sugam is the marketplace, Bima Vahak the women-led distribution channel and Bima Vistaar the combined rural product.

t: Postal Life Insurance, the oldest life insurance scheme still operating in India, was started in the year:
e: Postal Life Insurance began in 1884 as a welfare scheme for postal employees and was later extended to other government employees.

t: The requirement of 'consensus ad idem' in a contract means that:
o: The contract must be in writing
One party must be a company
Both parties understand the same thing in the same sense
e: Consensus ad idem (meeting of minds) is essential; a contract fails where the parties are at cross purposes about its subject matter.

t: The Insurance Ombudsman is required to pass an award within how long of receipt of all requirements from the complainant?
e: Rule 17 of the Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 requires the award within three months of receipt of all requirements.

t: An insurance web aggregator is an intermediary that:
o: Underwrites risks online on behalf of insurers
Displays and compares products of different insurers on a website and passes leads to insurers
Settles claims online for all insurers
e: Web aggregators provide price and feature comparison and lead generation; they do not underwrite or settle claims.

t: Under treaty reinsurance:
o: Each risk is offered and accepted individually
The insurer must cede and the reinsurer must accept all risks falling within the agreed class, automatically
The reinsurer can refuse any individual risk after a loss
Only life business can be reinsured
e: A treaty is an obligatory, standing agreement covering a defined portfolio, unlike facultative reinsurance which is arranged risk by risk.

t: The institution of Insurance Ombudsman in India was created by rules framed by the Central Government in:
e: The Redressal of Public Grievances Rules, 1998 created the Insurance Ombudsman; they were replaced by the Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017.

t: A disadvantage of quota share reinsurance for the ceding insurer is that:
o: The reinsurer can select only the worst risks
It gives no protection on any risk
It cedes a fixed share of even small risks that it could safely have retained
It is available only for marine business
e: Quota share cedes the same percentage of every risk regardless of size, so premium on small, retainable risks is given away.
